title: Why Direct Selling & Why Dayjoy?
objective: Help a new distributor articulate, honestly and without income promises, why direct selling and Dayjoy specifically can matter for a family's income and lifestyle.
content: Dayjoy positions direct selling as a 'parallel source of income' alongside a family's main income (F00003 page 3). The plan frames this around raising quality of life — better housing, education, family time — without stating that any specific extra amount is guaranteed. Dayjoy is a wellness brand under Adila Biotech, focused on wellness, beauty, agriculture, cloth, spices, and home care products (dayjoy_plan_faq_knowledge.csv, topic: company_story). When explaining 'why Dayjoy,' anchor on verifiable facts: Adila Biotech backing, ISO/GMP/WHO-GMP/FSSAI/HALAL/HACCP certifications, and North India manufacturing scale (dayjoy_company_knowledge.csv) — not on projected earnings.
examples: The plan's own slide language: 'A little extra income means no compromises, no tensions, happy family life, freedom and security' (F00003 page 3) — use as a values statement, not an earnings promise.
do_not_say: Do not state or imply any guaranteed, average, minimum, or typical income figure for any Dayjoy rank, activity, or team size (compensation_rules.csv row COMM-002: income is not guaranteed, and rows CONF-001/CONF-002/CONF-003 are unresolved conflicts — never state a specific Retail Profit %, Mentorship Incentive %, or Business Matching Incentive structure as confirmed fact). Do not make medical claims — no promises to cure, treat, prevent, or diagnose any disease or condition for any Dayjoy product beyond what is written on the approved product label/leaflet. Do not promise a specific rank-achievement timeline. Do not disparage competitor direct-selling companies. Do not claim regulatory/medical endorsement beyond Dayjoy's documented certifications (ISO, GMP, WHO-GMP, FSSAI, HALAL, HACCP). Do not present any figure from distributor_system_narrative_UNSTRUCTURED.md's compensation section as confirmed fact — it is UNVERIFIED.
quiz: Q: What does the compensation plan's own disclaimer (COMM-002) say about using this 'extra income' framing with a prospect? A: Any discussion of extra income must stay general — never attach a Rupee figure or guarantee, because actual income depends entirely on performance and downline size, and is never guaranteed.
source_ids: F00003 page 3; dayjoy_plan_faq_knowledge.csv (topics: plan_overview, why_direct_selling, company_story); compensation_rules.csv COMM-002
learning_outcomes: Distributor can explain the purpose of direct selling and Dayjoy's positioning without citing any income figure.
scenario: A prospect asks 'why should I do this instead of just staying at my job?' The distributor must answer using values/opportunity language only.
practice_task: Role-play a 60-second answer to 'why Dayjoy?' that contains zero Rupee figures.
common_mistakes: New distributors often reflexively quote a rank's Lifetime Reward amount from the rank table when asked 'why Dayjoy' — this is not appropriate for a first conversation and risks an income-claim compliance violation.
compliance_notes: Fully DAYJOY_SOURCED and safe to use as written — grounded only in company positioning and certification facts, not compensation figures.

title: Basics of Direct Selling Business
objective: Teach the mechanical basics of how a Dayjoy distributor operates: registration steps, DP vs MRP, and the core retail transaction.
content: Dayjoy describes four core steps to start the business: Register, Shop, Recommend, Replicate, requiring only a smartphone, internet, and ambition (F00003 page 4; JOIN-008 in compensation_rules.csv). The foundational transaction is retail sales: a distributor buys at Distributor Price (DP) and may resell at Maximum Retail Price (MRP), earning the difference (DEF-002, DEF-003 in compensation_rules.csv). The exact Retail Profit percentage is an unresolved conflict (CONF-001) — do not quote a specific %; instead explain the DP/MRP mechanic itself, which is fully verified.
examples: See compensation_examples.csv EX-001 for the one literal worked example in the source PDF (MRP Rs 5,000 / DP Rs 4,000) — present it only as 'here is one example the company itself printed,' never as a typical or guaranteed outcome.
do_not_say: Do not state or imply any guaranteed, average, minimum, or typical income figure for any Dayjoy rank, activity, or team size (compensation_rules.csv row COMM-002: income is not guaranteed, and rows CONF-001/CONF-002/CONF-003 are unresolved conflicts — never state a specific Retail Profit %, Mentorship Incentive %, or Business Matching Incentive structure as confirmed fact). Do not make medical claims — no promises to cure, treat, prevent, or diagnose any disease or condition for any Dayjoy product beyond what is written on the approved product label/leaflet. Do not promise a specific rank-achievement timeline. Do not disparage competitor direct-selling companies. Do not claim regulatory/medical endorsement beyond Dayjoy's documented certifications (ISO, GMP, WHO-GMP, FSSAI, HALAL, HACCP). Do not present any figure from distributor_system_narrative_UNSTRUCTURED.md's compensation section as confirmed fact — it is UNVERIFIED.
quiz: Q: What is the difference between DP and MRP? A: DP is what a distributor pays to purchase a product; MRP is the price at which it may be resold to a retail customer; the distributor's retail profit is the gap between the two, but the exact % is not yet a confirmed single figure (see CONF-001).
source_ids: F00003 page 4; compensation_rules.csv (JOIN-008, DEF-002, DEF-003, CONF-001); compensation_examples.csv EX-001
learning_outcomes: Distributor can describe the 4-step process and explain DP/MRP correctly, without stating a specific retail-margin percentage as fact.
scenario: A prospect asks 'how do I actually make money reselling products?'
practice_task: Practice explaining DP vs MRP using the EX-001 example, then explicitly state that the overall percentage range is still being confirmed.
common_mistakes: Quoting '30%' or '100%' retail profit as a settled fact — both figures exist in the source material but are in unresolved conflict (CONF-001).
compliance_notes: Fully DAYJOY_SOURCED; deliberately avoids stating a specific retail-profit % due to CONF-001.

title: Basic Business Plan Understanding
objective: Give distributors a correct, source-grounded mental model of the rank ladder and qualification requirements — without teaching them to calculate specific earnings.
content: Dayjoy's compensation plan is organized around 17 sequential Lifetime Reward Clubs, from Star Executive (Club 1) through Universal Ambassador (Club 17); rank is defined by the highest club achieved (compensation_rules.csv PROMO-001, PROMO-002, and the 17 RANK-* rows). Qualification depends on: two directly-introduced active distributors (QUAL-002), a monthly self-purchase requirement that scales by rank tier (ELIG-001 to ELIG-004), and the first BV-matching incentive being counted at a 1:2 or 2:1 ratio (QUAL-003). This lesson intentionally does NOT teach distributors to calculate a projected income — it teaches the qualification *structure* only, and explicitly flags that 3 core rate/structure fields (retail profit %, mentorship %, business-matching structure) remain unresolved conflicts that must never be used in a calculation (CONF-001/002/003).

quiz: Q: What two things does compensation_rules.csv say are required before a distributor can even qualify for Business Plan Payout?
